title: Numbers, time and dates
objectives: I can count from zero to one hundred and read out a phone number.
I can say how old I am and ask other people's age with ter.
I can ask for and tell the time, including half past, quarter past and on the dot.
I can name the days of the week and the months and say today's date.
I can say when a class, a meeting or a birthday is.

vocabulary.note: Feminine: uma. Two also changes: dois for masculine and duas for feminine.
Exactly one hundred is cem. For 101 to 199 the word changes to cento, as in cento e um.
Portuguese uses ter, not ser, to give your age: you have years.
Also used for age. The plural anos means years or years old.

example.pt: Qual é a idade da Ana?

vocabulary.note: Literally how many years. Used with ter.
The Brazilian word. In Portugal people say telemóvel.

example.pt: O número é oito, sete, seis, cinco.
example.en: The number is eight, seven, six, five.

vocabulary.note: Used in the plural to tell the time: São duas horas.
The plural horas and são are used even when the answer is one o'clock: É uma hora.

example.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

vocabulary.note: Used after the hour: três e meia is half past three. It also appears in meia hora, half an hour.
Used after the time to mean a.m.: oito da manhã.

example.en: It is nine in the morning.
It is three in the afternoon.

vocabulary.note: In everyday speech people often drop the -feira and just say segunda. The days from Monday to Friday are feminine.
Saturday and Sunday are masculine and have no -feira.
Months are written with a lower case letter in Portuguese.

example.pt: Qual é a data de hoje?

vocabulary.note: Used for the first day of a month only. All other days use the ordinary number.

example.en: Today is the first of May.

dialogues.title: Age and phone numbers
dialogues.context: Rafael and Beatriz meet at a party and exchange phone numbers.

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Oi, Beatriz! Quantos anos você tem?
lines.en: Hi, Beatriz! How old are you?

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Eu tenho vinte e oito anos. E você?
lines.en: I am twenty-eight. And you?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: I am thirty-two.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Qual é o seu celular, Rafael?
lines.en: What is your cell phone number, Rafael?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: É onze, nove, oito, sete, seis, cinco, quatro, três, dois, um.
lines.en: It is eleven, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.en: Sorry, what was that?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Onze, nove, oito, sete, seis, cinco, quatro, três, dois, um.
lines.en: Eleven, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Obrigada! O meu é onze, nove, oito, oito, quatro, quatro, três, três, dois, dois.
lines.en: Thank you! Mine is eleven, nine, eight, eight, four, four, three, three, two, two.

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: Great! Bye, Beatriz.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.en: Bye!

dialogues.title: What time is the class?
dialogues.context: Lucas and Mariana wait outside a classroom on a Monday morning.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.en: Hi, Mariana! What time is it?

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.en: It is half past nine.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: A aula é às dez, né?
lines.en: The class is at ten, right?

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: É, sim. Às dez em ponto.
lines.en: Yes. At ten on the dot.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.en: Then I have half an hour.

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.en: Exactly! I am sleepy.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.en: Me too! It is Monday.

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Amanhã a aula é à uma da tarde.
lines.en: Tomorrow the class is at one in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.en: At one in the afternoon? Great!

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.en: Bye, see you tomorrow!

dialogues.title: Today's date and birthdays
dialogues.context: Camila and Pedro are filling in a form at work and start talking about their birthdays.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.en: Camila, what day is it today?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Hoje é quarta-feira, primeiro de outubro.
lines.en: Today is Wednesday, the first of October.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.en: Wednesday! Then tomorrow is Thursday.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: É. Quando é o seu aniversário, Pedro?
lines.en: Yes. When is your birthday, Pedro?

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: É dia vinte e três de novembro. E o seu?
lines.en: It is the twenty-third of November. And yours?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: O meu é em janeiro, dia quinze.
lines.en: Mine is in January, on the fifteenth.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.en: January is summer in Brazil!

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.en: Yes! And July is winter.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Que legal, janeiro é um mês lindo!
lines.en: How cool, January is a lovely month!

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.en: Yes! And December too.

grammar.title: Cardinal numbers from 0 to 100
grammar.explanation:
The numbers from zero to ten are zero, um, dois, três, quatro, cinco, seis, sete, oito, nove and dez. Learn these first, because all the other numbers are built from them. From eleven to nineteen the forms are onze, doze, treze, catorze (also written quatorze), quinze, dezesseis, dezessete, dezoito and dezenove. Note the Brazilian spelling dezesseis and dezessete, which are written dezasseis and dezassete in Portugal.

The tens are vinte, trinta, quarenta, cinquenta, sessenta, setenta, oitenta and noventa. Between the tens you join the parts with e, meaning and: vinte e um, trinta e cinco, noventa e nove. The number one hundred is cem. Cento is used from 101 upward, as in cento e um.

The numbers one and two have a feminine form that agrees with the noun that follows: um dia but uma hora, dois meses but duas horas. The same happens inside compounds: vinte e uma horas, trinta e duas pessoas. All the other numbers up to one hundred do not change.

When you read a phone number, say the digits one by one, grouped as you like: onze, nove, oito, sete, seis, cinco, quatro, três, dois, um. In Brazil the first two digits are the area code, called DDD, and 11 is São Paulo. Many people say meia, short for meia dúzia or half a dozen, instead of seis when reading out phone numbers, to avoid confusion with other digits on a bad line.

examples.pt: Vinte e um, vinte e dois, vinte e três.
Trinta e cinco, quarenta e oito.
O número é nove, oito, sete, seis.
examples.en: The number is nine, eight, seven, six.

grammar.title: Ter in the present, and saying your age
grammar.explanation:
Ter means to have and is irregular. The forms are eu tenho, você tem, ele and ela tem, nós temos, a gente tem, vocês têm, and eles and elas têm. In the plural third person têm has a circumflex accent to separate it from the singular tem. In speech they sound almost the same, so the accent matters mainly in writing.

Portuguese gives age with ter, not with ser. You do not say I am thirty but I have thirty years: Eu tenho trinta anos. The question is Quantos anos você tem?, literally how many years do you have. The word anos must always be included. A short answer such as Trinta is possible in conversation, but the full sentence is Tenho trinta anos.

Ter is also used for many other things you have. Ter fome and ter sono are possible with the same meaning as estar com fome and estar com sono, and you will hear both. Meu and seu mean my and your and are shown here only inside fixed questions such as Qual é o seu celular?. They are explained fully in unit 5.

Questions are made with intonation, like all other yes or no questions in Portuguese: Você tem vinte anos? To negate, put não before the verb: Eu não tenho trinta anos.

rows: Ela tem vinte e dois anos.

examples.pt: Eu tenho vinte e cinco anos.
Ela tem trinta e um anos.

examples.en: I am not forty years old.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.explanation:
To ask the time, say Que horas são? The answer uses são and the plural horas for every hour except one: São duas horas, São dez horas. For one o'clock use the singular, É uma hora. Noon and midnight are also singular: É meio-dia, É meia-noite.

Add minutes with e: São três e dez is ten past three. The quarter hour is e quinze, and half past is e meia: São quatro e meia. To say before the hour, use menos: São três menos dez is ten to three. In speech you will also hear São dez para as três. For exactly on the hour say em ponto: São duas horas em ponto.

To say what part of the day you mean, add da manhã, da tarde or da noite after the time: São oito da manhã, São três da tarde, São dez da noite. The 24 hour clock is used in schedules and announcements: quatorze horas means two in the afternoon.

To say that something happens at a certain time, use às before the hour: A aula é às nove. The word às is the preposition a joined with the article as. For one o'clock, noon and midnight the form changes: à uma hora, ao meio-dia, à meia-noite. You write à with a grave accent, which marks the fusion of two a sounds.

examples.en: It is one in the afternoon.

examples.pt: São oito e meia da manhã.
examples.en: It is half past eight in the morning.

grammar.title: Days, months and dates
grammar.explanation:
The days of the week from Monday to Friday end in -feira: segunda-feira, terça-feira, quarta-feira, quinta-feira and sexta-feira. Saturday and Sunday are sábado and domingo. Days and months are not capitalized in Portuguese. In casual speech the -feira is often dropped: segunda, terça. The weekdays are feminine, so you say a segunda-feira and na segunda, while sábado and domingo are masculine: no sábado, no domingo. The words na and no mean em + a and em + o.

The months are janeiro, fevereiro, março, abril, maio, junho, julho, agosto, setembro, outubro, novembro and dezembro. To say in a month, use em: em março, em dezembro.

To ask for the date say Que dia é hoje? or Qual é a data de hoje? Answer with Hoje é dia cinco de maio, or Hoje é quinta-feira, cinco de maio. The word dia is optional. The first day of the month is the only one that uses an ordinal number: primeiro de maio. For all other days use the ordinary number: dois de maio, vinte e três de novembro. A date is written in the order day, month, year, so 3/4 is the third of April.

Because Brazil is in the southern hemisphere, the seasons are reversed compared with North America and Europe. The seasons are o verão, o outono, o inverno and a primavera. Summer runs roughly from December to March and winter from June to September.

examples.pt: Hoje é dia cinco de maio.
examples.en: Today is the fifth of May.
Today is the first of July.

examples.pt: Em julho é inverno no Brasil.
examples.en: In July it is winter in Brazil.

culture.title: Time, dates and phone numbers in Brazil
culture.text:
Brazilians write dates in the order day, month, year, so 03/04 is the third of April, not the fourth of March. Months and days are written in lower case. In everyday conversation time is usually said on the 12 hour clock with da manhã, da tarde or da noite, but train timetables, flight information, TV listings and many official notices use the 24 hour clock: dezenove horas means seven in the evening.

Punctuality is flexible in social situations. A party that starts at oito horas often fills up an hour or two later, and the expression hora brasileira jokingly describes this. At work, in class and for medical appointments you are expected to be on time, and em ponto means exactly that. Brazil abolished daylight saving time in 2019, so the clocks no longer change.

Phone numbers have a two digit area code, the DDD, followed by nine digits for cell phones, which always start with 9. Most people use WhatsApp to message, so asking Qual é o seu WhatsApp? is as common as asking for a phone number. The seasons are reversed relative to the northern hemisphere: Christmas in dezembro and New Year come in the middle of the summer, and Carnaval falls in February or early March, at the end of the hot season.

exercises.explanation: Quinze is fifteen. Cinquenta is fifty.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'It is one o'clock'?
exercises.explanation: One o'clock is singular: É uma hora. Hora is feminine, so it is uma.

exercises.prompt: What time is 'São duas e meia'?
exercises.explanation: Meia means half, so duas e meia is half past two.
Segunda-feira is Monday. Tuesday is terça-feira.
Quarenta is forty. Catorze is fourteen.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'the first of May'?
exercises.explanation: The first day of the month is the only one that uses an ordinal: primeiro de maio.

exercises.prompt: In Brazil, which season is it in January?
exercises.explanation: Brazil is in the southern hemisphere, so January is in the middle of summer.
Age uses ter, so the eu form is tenho.
The plural têm has a circumflex accent.
Hours are plural except for one o'clock.
Saturday comes after Friday and is called sábado.

answers: Eu tenho vinte e cinco anos.

The -feira is often dropped in everyday speech.

answers: O meu aniversário é em maio.
